# Near-misses for the two generic regex rules. Each is silent for a reason that
# belongs to the rule, which is the only kind of near-miss worth keeping: a line
# that stays quiet for an unrelated reason proves nothing about the pattern.
#
# 1. Lowercase. `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}` has no case-insensitive flag, so this is
#    silent BECAUSE of the character class. Make the regex case-insensitive and
#    it fires.
aws_access_key_id=akiaiosfodnn7example
# 2. Too short — eight characters after the prefix, not sixteen. Silent because
#    of the {16} quantifier; relax it and this fires.
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA1234
# 3. The prefix with nothing after it.
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA
# 4. A public key block and a certificate block. Both carry the `-----BEGIN`
#    frame the rule keys on, so they are silent BECAUSE the alternation demands
#    the word PRIVATE — drop it from the pattern and both fire.
-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
